Let <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> be sites. Let
<MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004>
be functors of the underlying categories such that <MATH_0005> is right adjoint to <MATH_0006>.
Lemma <REF_0001>
shows that if <MATH_0007> is continuous, then <MATH_0008> is cocontinous.
Conversely, if <MATH_0009> is cocontinuous, then we can't conclude that <MATH_0010>
is continuous. We will give an example of this phenomenon using
the big <ACCENT_0001>tale and smooth sites of a scheme, but presumably there is an
elementary example as well. Namely, consider a scheme <MATH_0011> and the sites
<MATH_0012> and <MATH_0013>. We may assume these
sites have the same underlying category, see
Topologies, Remark <REF_0002>.
Let <MATH_0014>. Then <MATH_0015> as a functor
from <MATH_0016> to <MATH_0017> is cocontinuous
as every smooth covering of a scheme can be refined by an <ACCENT_0002>tale
covering, see More on Morphisms, Lemma
<REF_0003>.
Conversely, the functor <MATH_0018> from <MATH_0019> to <MATH_0020>
is not continuous as a smooth covering is not an <ACCENT_0003>tale covering in general.
